newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish unemployment slows in February - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish unemployment slows in February - minister.

text.p: Polish unemployment rate fell in February 0.1 point to 13.4 percent and the drop, unusual for this time of year, bode well for cuts in the number of jobless in coming months, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said.
Registered unemployment fell by 23,845 people bringing the number of unemployed to 2.312 million from 2.336 in January.
"Employers signalled 60,000 openings, more than half of which were full-time jobs. More than 77 percent of them were from the private sector," Zielinski told a news conference.
"But the number is still too low," he added.
He said in February there were 3,000 more openings than in January and 2,500 more than at the end of February 1996.

The number of job loses due lay-offs fell by 4.5 percent against January to 163,000. Number of registered unemployed graduates, who account for three percent of all jobless, fell by 10 percent in January to 9,000.
Unemployment in the countryside fell by 4,600 or 0.4 percent in February.
